results.summary_before: This is a 16-bit Data General Nova 1200 CPU implemented with a 4-bit nibble-serial datapath, capable of executing programs stored in external QSPI Flash and using PSRAM for data storage. It includes a UART for serial communication at 19,200 baud and drives diagnostic blinkenlights on the 7-segment display. The design requires the official Tiny Tapeout QSPI PMOD for Flash and PSRAM, and programs are written in Nova assembly and flashed via a provided Python script. Notable features include full programmability and interactive terminal I/O, though it relies on external hardware for memory and communication.
results.summary: This design is an 8-bit shift register that scans a row of LEDs in a pattern reminiscent of a Cylon's visor. A direction flip-flop controls whether the lit bit moves left or right, and the direction reverses when the bit reaches either end. On reset, the first flip-flop is set while the others and the direction flip-flop are cleared. The eight outputs map directly to eight LEDs, producing a single sweeping light that bounces back and forth.
